headline: Ansys-fueled revenue surge masks GAAP earnings collapse
summary_short: Synopsys' Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 42% y/y to $2.28 billion, boosted by the Ansys acquisition, but GAAP EPS fell to $0.09 from $2.24 as intangible amortization, restructuring charges, and higher interest expense weighed on profit; non-GAAP EPS was $3.35, down 9% y/y.
summary_long: Revenue grew 42% y/y to $2.276B, driven by the Ansys acquisition consolidating into results and strength in Design Automation (up 62% y/y to $1.82B). GAAP operating income fell 68% y/y to $120.4M and diluted EPS dropped to $0.09 from $2.24, weighed down by $403.6M of acquired-intangible amortization, $115.9M of restructuring charges, and higher interest expense from Ansys deal financing. Non-GAAP diluted EPS was $3.35, down 9% y/y. Synopsys raised FY2026 revenue guidance to a $9.665B midpoint and non-GAAP EPS guidance to $14.76, citing cost discipline and integration synergies, partly offset by the pending Processor IP Solutions divestiture. Cash and short-term investments fell to $2.48B from $2.96B at fiscal year-end after $3.46B of debt repayment and $262.5M of buybacks.

drivers.explanation: Revenue growth reflects broad-based demand the CEO linked to AI-driven scaling of chip complexity, plus the Ansys business now embedded in the Design Automation segment; GAAP profit fell on acquisition-related amortization, restructuring, and financing costs tied to the Ansys deal.
Design Automation segment revenue (which the release defines as including Ansys products) rose to $1,821.8M, 80% of total revenue, from $1,122.3M (70%) a year ago.
Tracks revenue growth; cost of revenue also absorbed $248.4M of acquired-intangible amortization embedded in cost of revenue, up from $7.7M y/y, a direct effect of the Ansys acquisition.

GAAP operating expenses rose on $403.6M of total acquired-intangible amortization and $115.9M of restructuring charges (both newly disclosed line items post-Ansys), which more than offset revenue growth.

The company's own GAAP-to-non-GAAP reconciliation attributes the gap versus $643.7M non-GAAP net income to $403.6M of intangible amortization, $222.3M of stock-based compensation, and $115.9M of restructuring, partly offset by $138.8M of tax adjustments.
Tracks net income's decline, compounded by diluted share count rising to 192.1M from 156.1M y/y following Ansys-related equity issuance and a $2.0B common stock private placement.
Tracks net income's decline against a higher basic share count (191.5M vs 154.9M y/y) from Ansys-related equity issuance and the $2.0B private placement.
Non-GAAP net income rose to $643.7M from $572.7M, but the higher diluted share count (192.1M vs 156.1M) from Ansys-related equity issuance diluted per-share earnings despite the income growth.
